$comment: THE EDGE TRUST POLICY. One registry, two enforcers, one guard.
This file defines the only path by which an application API request may reach a backend, and
the controls that make that path provable rather than merely intended:
client -> Front Door + WAF -> APIM -> backend
APIM is the identity/trust boundary. It is the only place a token is validated and the only
place the closed X-Idp-* contract comes into existence. Backends consume that contract and
never re-derive it.
WHAT THIS FILE NO LONGER DEFINES, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. The apim-to-backend hop once
carried a second, application-level control: APIM presented a client certificate, ingress
validated it and republished its hash, and each backend refused any request whose forwarded
hash was not allow-listed. That mechanism is DEFERRED in full - see
docs/adr/0008-defer-certificate-based-gateway-to-backend-provenance.md - and NOTHING
REPLACED IT. Not a shared secret, not an API key, not a header, not a token.
The consequence is recorded here rather than left to be discovered: that hop now rests on
network placement alone. Internal ingress admits anything already inside the environment - a
compromised sidecar, a misconfigured job, a second container app - and a backend consuming
the X-Idp-* contract as authoritative will believe such a caller. The specification's own
position is that network placement alone is not sufficient proof (spec.md FR-IDENT-012),
which is why that requirement is now marked DEFERRED there too rather than quietly satisfied.
VALIDATED BY:
dotnet/tests/Synthia.ArchitectureTests/EdgeTrustPolicyTests.cs
ragcore/tests/security/test_edge_trust_policy.py
build/scripts/check-edge-path.sh  (proven to fail by verify-edge-guard.sh)

chain.statement: Every application API request traverses Front Door + WAF, then APIM, then the backend. There is no other path, including for service-to-service and Workload calls (spec 13.4).

hops.networkControl: Front Door is the only public DNS name and the only public IP. Backends have no public ingress.
hops.applicationControl: WAF managed rule sets and rate limiting. TLS 1.2 minimum, HTTPS-only.
hops.$comment: Boundary 1 in spec 10.2. Nothing is trusted here; all input is hostile until validated.

hops.networkControl: APIM accepts origin traffic only from the AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag; every other source is denied by NSG and by APIM's own network configuration.
hops.applicationControl: APIM rejects any request whose X-Azure-FDID does not equal this platform's Front Door identifier.
$comment: The service tag alone is insufficient: it admits EVERY Azure customer's Front Door,
so an attacker provisions their own profile and points it at this origin. The FDID
check is what makes the origin specific to this platform. Neither control is
sufficient alone (spec 10.3) - this is the pair that sentence names.

hops.networkControl: Container Apps ingress is internal on every application container app; external ingress is prohibited. The backend has no public FQDN and is reachable only from inside the environment's VNet, into which APIM is injected.
$comment: THIS IS THE ONE HOP WITH A SINGLE CONTROL, and that is a known gap rather than a design.
Every other hop in this file carries two independent controls because neither a network
control nor an application control is sufficient alone. Here the application control is
deferred (ADR 0008) and nothing replaced it, so the hop carries the network control only.
VNet injection admits anything already inside the VNet - a compromised sidecar, a
misconfigured job, a second container app - and each of those can mint any tenant and any
role it likes, because the backends consume X-Idp-* as authoritative and can no longer
tell an APIM-stamped contract from one a caller typed.
Do not close this by adding a shared secret, an API key or a bearer header. Those were
considered and rejected in the ADR: a secret in a header is replayable by anyone who sees
it once and appears in every log that captures headers.

deferred.mechanism: APIM client certificate, validated by Container Apps ingress and republished as a forwarded certificate hash that each backend checked against an allow-list.
deferred.reEntryCondition: The architecture/security decision in ADR 0008 must be revisited and explicitly approved before any gateway-to-backend provenance mechanism is implemented.

identityContract.statement: The closed Gateway-derived header contract (spec 11.5). APIM deletes any inbound copy before validation and sets these on the outbound request. Backends consume them and MUST NOT parse a token.
$comment: CLOSED means five, exactly. A sixth header carrying authority is a second identity
derivation wearing a different name, and the enforcers assert the list length so that
adding one requires editing this file rather than editing one service.

audiences.roles: non-empty subset of administrator, senior_technician, technician

neverParseTokens.statement: No backend validates, decodes or inspects a bearer token. There is no JWT library on the audience path and no signing key to rotate at this tier.

neverTrustClientAssertedAuthority.statement: Tenant, role, audience, principal and impersonation targets are never accepted from a client field, in any position - header, query parameter, path segment or body.
$comment: Compared with case folded and separators stripped, so tenant_id, tenantId, X-Tenant-Id
and TENANT-ID are one entry rather than four somebody has to remember.
ONE EXCEPTION, and it is a narrowing: tenantId as a read filter on the staff audience.
It selects within the set the caller may already see and confers nothing; the tenant
query filter still applies underneath it, so a value outside that set returns no rows.

rejectSpoofedIdentity.statement: DEFERRED. No backend can currently distinguish an X-Idp-* contract set by APIM from one supplied by a caller that reached it directly, and none refuses on that basis.
$comment: WHAT STILL HOLDS. APIM deletes every inbound copy of the contract before validation, so a
caller arriving from the internet cannot smuggle one through the gateway. That control is
unchanged and is asserted by check-edge-path.sh and both stacks' edge trust tests.
WHAT NO LONGER HOLDS. A caller positioned INSIDE the environment bypasses APIM entirely
and the backend will honour whatever X-Idp-* contract it presents. That was the case this
rule existed to cover, and it is open.

noExternalIngress.statement: No application container app declares external ingress. This is the network half of the apim-to-backend hop and is asserted against the committed manifests.

noDirectServiceToService.statement: A service MUST NOT call another platform service by its internal address (spec 13.4). Cross-service application calls go out through the approved egress path and back in through Front Door and APIM.
